title: Council endorses ION rapid transit extension to Cambridge
subtitle: Enbridge franchise talks, deferred green building standard, Mooregate housing, return-to-office motions, farm signs and taxi incentives
overview: Council endorsed a full-length light rail extension from Fairway Station in Kitchener to Downtown Cambridge and directed staff to seek full provincial and federal funding {{vote:m9}}. The same motion revised the by-law on farm accessory signs along Regional roads. Council deferred a proposal to require a zero-carbon design standard for new Regional buildings until March 10, 2026 {{vote:m7}}.

Council authorized staff to negotiate changes to the Enbridge Gas franchise agreement, which expires on May 24, 2026, and to take part in an Ontario Energy Board hearing {{vote:m15}}. It asked staff to report by the end of Q1 2026 on ways to fund Mooregate housing construction, and referred funding for A Better Tent City to the 2026 budget process {{vote:m11}}. The overnight accessible taxi incentive rises to $10 per trip from January 1, 2026 {{vote:m13}}.

A proposed corporate facilities strategic plan, linked to the return-to-office policy, was defeated {{vote:m19}}. A separate motion to pause further return-to-office activity was also defeated {{vote:m22}}. Council scheduled a closed meeting for November 21 on legal advice about litigation over the 100 Victoria Street encampment.

decisions.item: Rapid transit to Cambridge and farm signs
decisions.detail: Council endorsed a full-length LRT extension from Fairway Station to Downtown Cambridge, directed staff to pursue full senior-government funding, and revised the farm accessory sign rules in By-law 10-030.

Council deferred the proposal to replace the LEED Silver standard with the Zero Carbon Building-Design standard to the March 10, 2026 Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee meeting, along with requested information.

Council authorized staff to negotiate changes to the draft model franchise agreement, take part in the Ontario Energy Board hearing, and support provincial changes allowing fees for use of the right of way.

decisions.item: Housing, tent city funding and public art
decisions.detail: Council approved artwork for the Langs Drive redevelopment, referred continued $236,390 annual funding for A Better Tent City to budget, and requested a report on funding to advance Mooregate construction.
Council amended the Taxi By-law, doubled the overnight accessible taxi incentive to $10 per trip from January 1, 2026, and asked staff to propose an overnight accessible van pilot.
Council approved the 2026 Library operating budget with a net levy of $3,359,983, the capital budget and forecast, and the 2026 Library Business Plan.
Council accepted a $324,950 tender for the roof replacement and added $95,000 to the 2026 capital budget from library and facilities reserves.
Council defeated the notice of motion to develop a corporate facilities strategic plan and facilities business plan.
